subject: Post-demo: model fit & multilingual eval plan (EU/APAC focus)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sophie Müller <sophie.muller@globexretail.de>, Kenji Tanaka <kenji.tanaka@apacretail.co.jp>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: model fit & multilingual eval plan (EU/APAC focus)

Thanks again for the time today — great conversation and very helpful context on the regional QA needs. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we run the eval canary:

Recap:
- Primary use cases: automated product copy localization, customer support triage in DE/FR/JA/KO, and intent classification for Nordic languages (DE/FR/JAP/KO mention).
- Key constraints: strict latency target for web chat (<= 200ms avg token), EU data residency for a subset of telemetry, and high precision for categorical intents (F1 > 0.88).

Recommended initial model candidates (for eval):
- redwood-medium-xlq (quantized, production-friendly tradeoff: lower cost, good latency)
- open-large-v2 (strong generalization; baseline for quality)
- xgen-multilingual-7b (good on APAC languages in our benchmarks)

Attachments I’m sharing: Globex_Eval_Prompt_Set_v1.csv (prompt sets + desired labels), redwood_regional_benchmarks.pdf (summary of our baseline scores by language). Please add your regional testsets if you want us to run against them.

Suggested evaluation plan & timeline:
1) You share regional test sets (DE/FR/NL for EU, JA/KO/EN for APAC) — ideally ~1k examples per language with labels.
2) Redwood runs a 3-day canary across the three model candidates with: latency/throughput measurement, quality metrics (accuracy, F1, hallucination rate), and regression detection against your golden set.
3) We’ll present a short readout and recommend a rollout (canary -> canary+fallback -> GA).

Questions / asks for Globex team:
- Can you confirm the expected data residency requirements for the EU test artifacts?
- Are there any tokenization or pre/post-processing rules we should apply for Japanese/Korean?
- Who should we include on the eval results readout (ops, legal)?

Next steps:
- Sophie / Kenji: share region-specific test sets and any non-standard tokenization rules by EOD Friday (2027-06-04).
- We’ll kick off the canary on Monday (2027-06-07) and aim to have a readout by Thursday (2027-06-10).

Thanks — I’ll schedule the readout and include the benchmark dashboard link once the run starts.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0197

Attachments:
- Globex_Eval_Prompt_Set_v1.csv (prompt templates + expected labels)
- redwood_regional_benchmarks.pdf (summary)

From: Sophie Müller <sophie.muller@globexretail.de>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 12:30:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Post-demo: model fit & multilingual eval plan (EU/APAC focus)

Hi Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. Quick clarifications from our side and a small request: 

1) Test sets: attaching our regional file (globex_regional_testset_v2.csv) — contains ~1.2k labeled examples split across DE/FR/NL and a small EN control set.
2) Data residency: for the EU test artifacts we need the evaluation to run within the Frankfurt region for any telemetry or logs that contain customer PII — is that supported in the canary configuration?
3) Hallucination/regression: in our last vendor POC we saw regressions when we moved from 13B -> 7B quantized that affected product-spec accuracy. Can you include a simple hallucination metric (percentage of responses with fabricated facts vs. golden) in the readout?

Also — can you confirm which tokenizer (and vocabulary) you’d use for Japanese? We had token-splitting differences that affected intent parsing.

If you can answer the residency + tokenizer question we’ll confirm people for the readout and any legal watchers.

Sophie
Sophie Müller
Senior Product Manager, NLP | Globex Retail
sophie.muller@globexretail.de

Attachment:
- globex_regional_testset_v2.csv (sampled and labeled)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Sophie Müller <sophie.muller@globexretail.de>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 18:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: model fit & multilingual eval plan (EU/APAC focus)

Thanks, Sophie — quick technical notes: 

- EU residency: we can run the canary entirely in eu-west-1 (Frankfurt region) using the private evaluation pool; logs that contain PII can be restricted to customer-managed KMS and retained per your policy. I’ll coordinate an ops runbook if you confirm the retention window.
- Tokenizer: for Japanese we’ll use the SentencePiece model that’s bundled with xgen-multilingual-7b by default; if you have a custom tokenizer mapping we can plug that in as a pre-processing step to ensure tokenization parity. Please attach any mapping or examples.
- Hallucination metric: we’ll compute a coarse hallucination rate using a set of golden facts per item and a simple string-match/NER-backed heuristic. We’ll also flag examples for manual review where the model returns high-confidence but non-overlapping entities.
- Latency: to meet <=200ms avg token for web chat we recommend redwood-medium-xlq with batching window tuned to 15ms and async streaming enabled; if latency SLA is stricter we can provision a higher-tier dedicated pool for the canary.

Planned artifacts from Redwood after the run:
- Per-language accuracy/F1, confusion matrices for intents, hallucination rate, latency distribution, and per-route cost estimate.

I’ll start the Frankfurt pool prep once we have the legal/data-residency confirmation from Globex.

-rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com

Attachment referenced:
- redwood_regional_benchmarks.pdf (detailed figures)

From: Kenji Tanaka <kenji.tanaka@apacretail.co.jp>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Sophie Müller <sophie.muller@globexretail.de>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Jun 2027 23:05:00 +0900
Subject: Re: Post-demo: model fit & multilingual eval plan (EU/APAC focus)

Hi all — thanks for the plan. A couple quick points from APAC QA: 

- Tokenization: we have an internal token-normalization step for Japanese that merges uncommon kana variants — I’ll attach an example mapping in a follow-up, but we’d like Redwood to apply that as a pre-processing step during the canary.
- Schedule: the team is okay with the Monday canary start (2027-06-07) — can we do a 48-hour holdback on the APAC test set so we can do an internal blind review before you publish results?
- Please include a short section in the readout about fallback behavior (if the quantized model drops below quality threshold, how the system will route to open-large-v2).

FWIW forwarding Sophie’s testset and Marissa’s prompt set to our ops for visibility.

Kenji Tanaka
Head of AI Platforms | APAC Retail Group
kenji.tanaka@apacretail.co.jp
